title: Ifor and the Little Yellow Peep
markdown:
Once upon a time, in a room that smelled faintly of warm sunshine and cookies baking — a smell that made tummies rumble a happy rumble — lived Ifor the teddy bear. Curtains breathed. Dust motes drifted like slow gold. Ifor was a most excellent napper. He could nap through a marching band next door, through a flock of geese overhead, and even through a sneeze that sounded like a tiny earthquake. His fur was the colour of toasted marshmallows, soft and huggable. His round button eyes blinked very, very slowly. Each blink felt like a little decision. He spent his days snoozing in a warm sunny patch on the carpet, dreaming of rivers of honey and quiet afternoons where nothing much happened. That was exactly how Ifor liked it.

Every day he shared the cozy room with Elsie. Elsie was a budgie, a tiny bright puff of blue feathers who flitted and fluttered and sang with all her might. Her songs were like little tinkling bells dipped in sunshine: happy chirps, bubbly trills, and whistles that made toes want to tap. Ifor loved Elsie’s singing, even though he was a quiet-thinker, a slow-and-steady sort of bear. Sometimes, watching her zip about like a little blue lightning bolt, he gave a tiny sigh. He wished for a friend who was just… well, his size. A friend for quiet games, like stacking little pebbles, or for sharing big thoughts, like why clouds look like fluffy sheep.

Until one day, tick-tick-tick went a tiny tapping on the windowpane. Ifor’s button eyes widened as much as button eyes can. Elsie, practising a tricky high note, stopped mid-trill with a little eep. Perched on the windowsill, looking like a ball of dandelion fluff that had learned to balance, was a tiny chick, all yellow and so fluffy he might float away on a breeze. His round curious eyes looked a little watery. This was Pip.

Pip looked at Ifor’s big warm fuzz, then at Elsie’s flash of cheerful blue, and let out a tiny sad peep, like a question mark filled with longing. Ifor’s chest tightened. “Oh dear,” he whispered, a low rumble that felt like a gentle hug wrapping the room. Elsie fluttered to Ifor’s shoulder, her usual cheer a little softer. “He looks a bit lonely, doesn’t he?” Pip peeped again. His fluffy chest puffed with a wobbly breath. He missed his mummy, who gave the best cuddles. He missed his daddy, who had the warmest voice. He missed his brothers and sisters, who always played chase. He missed the big warm straw-filled nest where everyone snuggled together. It was all so new and strange, and Pip felt very homesick. His little yellow head drooped.

Because of that, Ifor’s bear-brain, usually full of nap schedules, sparked. “We need to make him a nest,” he said, puffing his chest a tiny bit. Elsie bobbed so fast her feathers ruffled. “A super-duper cozy nest. I know. A nest shaped like a pillow. A nest-pillow. That way he can take it anywhere.” Ifor thought that simply brilliant. A nest-pillow would be soft and snuggly, like a warm hug, and it would feel like home no matter where Pip sat.

Because of that, they set to work. Ifor, with big strong gentle arms, collected the softest things in the room: a fluffy white feather that might have fallen from a cloud, a bit of creamy woolly yarn that had snuggled out of a knitting basket, and the very softest stuffing from a forgotten old cushion that had seen better days. Elsie, small and nimble, was chief fluff-gatherer. She zipped like a tiny blue hummingbird, bringing wisps of cotton wool that danced in the air and bits of fuzz that tickled Ifor’s nose. Ifor arranged everything on the floor, plump and squishy, testing each handful against his own marshmallow fur. While they worked, Pip sat nearby and, in little chirps and peeps and soft sighs, told Ifor about his home and how much he missed it. Ifor did not interrupt. He sat and listened, nodding his fuzzy head, kind button eyes showing he understood every chirp, even the ones that wobbled. Pip was not alone with his feelings.

Because of that, Elsie decided the nest-pillow needed happy music. She sang her brightest songs, like a tiny music box winding up: sunny meadows, tasty seeds, families snuggled together. Then she spotted something glinting under the edge of the rug. A bright shiny red button, perfectly round and wonderfully smooth. She nudged it out and tucked it in the middle of the pillow. “For good luck,” she chirped. “And to make it sparkle like a little berry.” Ifor’s sunny carpet patch was waiting. His nap schedule whispered. He stayed. He smoothed the last bit of fluff and patted the pillow into a lovely plump shape. Soft. Warm. Bursting with friendship. Skipping the nap was the hardest choice a champion napper could make, and he made it.

Until finally, Pip hopped toward the nest-pillow. He sniffed with his little beak, then nudged it. The red button winked like a berry. Then, with a happy sigh that puffed his yellow chest, he snuggled right down in the middle. He tucked his fluffy head under his wing, eyes closing like tiny sleepy moons. He felt safe. He felt warm. He felt loved, as if he were back in his own cozy nest. Ifor and Elsie watched, a warm fuzzy feeling spreading from the tips of Ifor’s ears to the smallest of Elsie’s tail feathers. Pip was no longer so homesick. They had made a nest, and they had made a friend.

Ever since then, Ifor still napped in his sunny patch, only now a small fluffy yellow friend napped nearby, and the naps were even sweeter.
